person_note: The quote set repeatedly shows a nonparticipating narrator moving among characters and reporting the private thoughts of Johann Clement, Karen, Kitty, Ari, Jossi, and Sarah, alongside broad historical exposition. First- and second-person forms occur only in dialogue, aphorism, embedded biblical language, or character reflection, not in controlling narration. The independent scholarly structural description and two explicit whole-book study-guide descriptions agree that the novel is third-person, while the curated Chapter Nineteen excerpt locally corroborates that form. No research source indicated alternating or constitutive first-person sections. The principal limitation is that the accessible authorized excerpt is short, but the extensive diagnostic quotes and whole-book structural evidence make the classification high-confidence THIRD.
